articles.headline: European soccer live updates: Man City, Liverpool in action
articles.description: The European soccer weekend continues with Man City looking to go clear at the top of the Premier League vs. Sunderland, and Liverpool facing Bournemouth.
articles.body:
The weekend of soccer across Europe continues!

In the Premier League, Liverpool travel to take on AFC Bournemouth while Manchester City, coming off their Manchester derby win, can go three points clear of champions Arsenal at the top of the table with a home win over Sunderland. Later, Manchester United visit Fulham as they look to bounce back after losing the derby and getting eliminated midweek in the Carabao Cup.

In LaLiga, Atlético Madrid host Real Madrid in the first Madrid derby of the season, while Juventus meet Atalanta in Serie A. In the Bundesliga, Bayer Leverkusen face RB Leipzig before the day concludes in Ligue 1 with Marseille hosting Paris Saint-Germain in Le Classique.

Enjoy all the updates from Sunday's matches.

articles.headline: Broncos remain confident in OC Davis Webb as playcaller
articles.description: The Broncos maintain a "high level of confidence and comfort" in Davis Webb as their offensive playcaller, a team source told ESPN.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos maintain a "high level of confidence and comfort" in Davis Webb as their offensive playcaller, a team source told ESPN.

The Broncos struggled in their season debut under Webb as offensive coordinator last Monday in Kansas City, managing just 176 yards from scrimmage in their 31-10 loss to the Chiefs.

But Broncos head coach Sean Payton continues to support Webb and stand by the first-year offensive coordinator, believing he will be a successful playcaller.

Payton defended Webb last week, saying the Broncos' entire offensive operation should shoulder some blame for Monday's performance.

"I think that game didn't go for any of us as we would've hoped," Payton said Thursday. "Right? I mean, I said in the meeting this morning: There was dirt on a ton of people's hands, starting with me.

"So we've got to learn from that. It's a quick turnaround, you can't get to the next game quick enough, and I'm sure it's the same way for [Webb]."

Webb emerged as a head-coaching candidate this past offseason and interviewed for open positions with the Las Vegas Raiders, Buffalo Bills and Baltimore Ravens. He also had opportunities to become an offensive coordinator on other teams, according to sources.

The Broncos ultimately kept Webb, promoting him from quarterbacks coach to offensive coordinator in February.

Broncos quarterback Bo Nix struggled mightily in Kansas City, fumbling three times (losing one) and throwing an interception while also being sacked a career-high four times.

Nix was asked Thursday what Denver's offense needed to do to make it easier on Webb in Week 2. The third-year quarterback paused briefly and got right to the point: "Get first downs, score points."

The Broncos return home in Week 2 to host the Jacksonville Jaguars, who rolled to a 34-20 victory last season in Denver.

articles.headline: Browns expected to evaluate QB situation ahead of Week 3
articles.description: The Browns are expected to evaluate their quarterback situation after their Week 2 game against the Buccaneers.
articles.body:
Decision time is coming for the Cleveland Browns and their quarterback situation.

Deshaun Watson will make his second straight start on the road to open the season for the Browns -- and after that, Cleveland will make its evaluation.

While no firm decision has been made for Week 3, the belief is that the first two games would serve as a natural evaluation point. In other words, the Browns could use the return to Cleveland for their Week 3 home opener and a two-game sample size as the impetus for a quarterback change.

Shedeur Sanders would be the next man up.

Watson earned the right to start the first two weeks with his play in camp and his experience. But Cleveland's offensive game operation in Week 1 left those in the building frustrated. The performance all around -- not just from Watson -- wasn't great in the 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The reality is that Watson will help inform the decision moving forward with his play Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. If Watson plays well and leads Cleveland to a victory, the Browns have an easy decision. If it does not go well for Watson in a loss, a change could be coming.

The middle ground is the area where it's less clear.

The Browns need to come out of this season knowing whether they have a franchise quarterback on their roster. With multiple first-round picks in the 2027 draft, Cleveland is among the teams in the mix for one of the top college quarterbacks.

If it doesn't look like Watson is a major part of their future moving forward, the Browns need to see whether Sanders is. The fuller the look, the better.

After last week, when Watson went 16-of-22 for 205 yards with a touchdown and an interception, Browns coach Todd Monken told reporters he anticipated sticking with Watson. Monken later said the game tape confirmed his decision.

Watson did play better in the second half against Jacksonville, and perhaps getting his feet wet after not playing in the regular season since 2024 will lead to a more consistent performance Sunday.

"We got to play better around him," Monken said. "We got to call it better, and he's got to play better."

articles.headline: Sources: Steelers eye Week 3 return for CB Joey Porter Jr.
articles.description: The Steelers are planning for Joey Porter Jr. to potentially return for their Week 3 game against the Bengals, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are planning for Joey Porter Jr., who has missed the first two games of the season, to potentially return for their Week 3 game against the Cincinnati Bengals, sources told ESPN.

But whether or not Porter actually does return is a bit more ambiguous and is connected to the star cornerback's back injury and conditioning level.

Porter's back, according to a source, has "flared up when he's tried to go full speed, and they haven't been able to get it where it needs to be." Porter has been considering getting a second opinion on his back.

The results of a second medical opinion would help determine whether the Steelers get their wish to have their standout cornerback back in time to match up with Bengals wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins next weekend.

The Steelers might think, as one source described this week, that Porter is "fired up about playing against Cincinnati," but there is a business angle to this situation that cannot be ignored as the sides remain at an impasse in contract discussions.

The Steelers, as a rule, don't negotiate in-season contract extensions. Porter believes he is worthy of a lucrative new deal, the likes of which assorted teammates have signed during the offseason. But the two sides haven't gotten close to an agreement, which has brought the possibility of a trade into play.

For now, the Steelers think Porter could be back next Sunday. Others think Porter's back still needs attention -- and the story that has lingered throughout the offseason is continuing on unabated two weeks into the regular season.

Porter, 26, was ruled out for this Sunday's road game against the New England Patriots after being listed as limited in practice all week. The four-year veteran left Thursday's practice early with a team trainer.

Porter's teammates have continued to support him and say his situation hasn't been a distraction inside the locker room.

"I'm with Joe, whatever he's doing -- whether it's injury, whether it's contract, whatever it is, I respect it," Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen said Thursday. "I'm behind him 100%. I tell him every single time, 'I respect how you go about your business every single day.'"

articles.headline: Sources: Colts' Keenan Allen faces minimum 3-game suspension
articles.description: Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen, who was formally charged last week with two misdemeanor offenses stemming from his drunken driving arrest in downtown Indianapolis last month, is facing a minimum three-game suspension, sources told ESPN.
articles.body:
Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen, who was formally charged Tuesday with two misdemeanor offenses stemming from his drunken driving arrest in downtown Indianapolis last month, is facing a minimum three-game suspension from the NFL, league sources told ESPN.

Three-game suspensions are mandated by the NFL's collective bargaining agreement, which also stipulates that suspensions could be longer if a player is intoxicated at higher levels.

Police officers on the scene when Allen was arrested Aug. 30 said they received a .224 blood-alcohol level reading from the veteran wide receiver -- nearly three times the legal limit, meaning the NFL could decide to increase the three-game ban that he is already facing.

According to a probable cause affidavit obtained by ESPN's Stephen Holder, Allen's blood-alcohol level triggered a more serious Class A misdemeanor charge, per Indiana law.

An Indianapolis police sergeant encountered Allen at 1 a.m. after conducting a traffic investigation. Allen, according to the police report, was parked in a no-parking zone, prompting the officer to address the situation. The officer stated he smelled a strong odor of alcohol when he went to speak to Allen.

Allen is not expected to miss playing time while the case proceeds through the courts. Coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that the Colts are allowing the legal process to play out.

The NFL is expected to wait for Allen's legal case to conclude before it proceeds with any potential discipline. The next event on the docket in the case, an attorney conference, is scheduled for Oct. 26.

Allen, 34, joined the Colts in August on a one-year deal. The six-time Pro Bowler had six catches for 32 yards in the Colts' Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 2 Buzz

Biggest concerns heading into Week 2

Players with early starts

Joe Burrow, QB, Bengals (back): Burrow is dealing with back soreness and is listed as questionable but is expected to start. The quarterback stated that it would be "ridiculous" if the injury caused him to miss Week 2. Even in a tough matchup like the Texans, Burrow is a fantasy QB1.

If you want to avoid the matchup, Jaxson Dart and Brock Purdy are realistic options that a fantasy manager could have backing up Burrow. If you're skittish, those two could be started over him. However, for most of you, the choice should be to ride with Burrow.

TreVeyon Henderson, RB, Patriots (ankle): After missing the Patriots' opener because of an ankle injury, Henderson returned to practice this week and says he is "ready to go" for Week 2. Henderson will share work in the backfield with Rhamondre Stevenson. However, he is the more explosive option and therefore brings more fantasy upside.

Henderson can be played over Quinshon Judkins, MarShawn Lloyd, Tony Pollard, J.K. Dobbins, Rico Dowdle, Blake Corum, Kenny Gainwell and Jonathon Brooks.

Jalen Coker, WR, Panthers (ankle): After a huge Week 1 performance, Coker was limited in practice to start the week because of an ankle injury. He was able to log a full practice Friday and was removed from the injury report, meaning he will play in Week 2. While the Panthers will not often have "scorefests" like they did in Week 1, Coker's usage jumps off the screen. He saw nine targets -- three of the deep variety -- and finished with 138 yards and a touchdown, while narrowly missing a second score.

Coker is a high upside WR3. You can feel comfortable playing him over DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman Jr, Alec Pierce, Marvin Harrison Jr and Chris Godwin Jr.

Alvin Kamara, RB, Saints (knee): Kamara has "moved well" at practice and Kellen Moore has said he should play this week. He is a flex option that brings some PPR upside, but also some risk as we do not know how much work he will see. Sept. 20: Sunday's news to know

By Todd Zola

The penultimate Sunday of the regular season gets going at 1:10 p.m. ET with the New York Mets hosting the Philadelphia Phillies. This is one of a few contests that may have to deal with rain. Both clubs have Monday off, howver, if conditions prohibit playing the game and there's a need to reschedule. 

Other matchups under any kind of "weather watch" include the Pittsburgh Pirates at the Kansas City Royals, the Athletics at the Cleveland Guardians and the Detroit Tigers at the Chicago White Sox. Fortunately, none of these six teams are slated to play on Monday either, so the same "wiggle room" applies.

The Boston Red Sox are rearranging their rotation to line up for their likely wild-card series. This pushes Payton Tolle to Tuesday, with Patrick Sandoval taking the hill this afternoon in the rubber game against the Tampa Bay Rays.  

Bryce Eldridge is in the league's concussion protocol and will miss today's NL West matchup between the San Francisco Giants and Los Angeles Dodgers. He reportedly bumped his head at the team hotel. Brett Harris will likely fill in at first base.

Kyle Tucker left yesterday's contest in the seventh inning after fouling a ball off his leg. The Dodgers were ahead by six runs at the time and manager Dave Roberts indicated that the score helped in the decision. He's hopeful that the outfielder will play today. It's been a frustrating year for Tucker, but he's doing his best to salvage the season with a .327/.424/.796 line over his last 15 games.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Sunday. 

Sept. 19: Saturday's news to know

By Todd Zola

Today's action starts a bit earlier than initially scheduled, with the Windy City doubling as Rainy City.
